description: A deeply savoury Kenyan beef stew where onions are cooked down until sweet and golden, forming the backbone of a rich, glossy gravy.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef cubes in batches over high heat. Remove and set aside.
Add the sliced onions to the same pot and cook on medium-low heat for 10–12 minutes until soft, golden and sweet.
Stir in the garlic and chopped tomatoes (if using) and cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Return the beef to the pot, add salt and water, cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until the beef is tender and the gravy is thick.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with ugali or rice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and sukuma wiki.

description: A rich Kenyan beef stew with soft potatoes, slow-cooked in a tomato and onion sauce. A family favourite served with ugali or rice.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a heavy pot. Brown the beef cubes in batches over high heat. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, fry onions until golden. Add garlic and curry powder, stir for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and cook until they form a thick sauce. Return the beef to the pot.
Add water, cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes. Add potatoes and cook for a further 20 minutes until both beef and potatoes are tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with ugali or rice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali, rice or chapati and a side of kachumbari.

description: Tender beef simmered in a bright, tangy tomato sauce—a simple Kenyan weeknight dish that lets the tomatoes shine.

steps.instruction: Boil the beef with salt and water until tender, about 30 minutes. Reserve the broth.
Heat oil and sauté the onion (if using) until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook on medium heat for 10–12 minutes until they collapse into a thick sauce.
Add the boiled beef and a splash of reserved broth. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce coats the meat. Adjust salt and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice, ugali or chapati.

name_en: Kenyan Goat Meat and Onion Stew
description: A hearty Kenyan goat stew where generous amounts of onion melt into the sauce, balancing the rich, gamey flavour of the meat.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a heavy pot and brown the goat meat on all sides for 8–10 minutes.
Add the sliced onions and cook on medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic and tomatoes (if using) and cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes soften.
Add salt and water, cover tightly and simmer on low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours until the meat is very tender and the sauce has thickened.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with ugali or rice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and kachumbari.

description: Chicken pieces cooked in a vibrant tomato sauce with onions and garlic—a simple, comforting Kenyan chicken dish.

steps.instruction: Boil the chicken pieces with salt and water until tender, about 25 minutes. Reserve the broth.
Heat oil and sauté the onions until soft and golden. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook on medium heat for 10 minutes until they form a rich sauce.
Add the boiled chicken and a little reserved broth. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until the chicken is coated in the sauce. Adjust salt and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice, ugali or chapati.

description: A rustic Kenyan chicken stew built on a generous base of slow-cooked onions, garlic and a touch of tomato.

steps.instruction: Brown the chicken pieces in hot oil for 6–8 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Add the sliced onions to the pot and cook on medium-low heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic and tomatoes (if using) and cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Return the chicken to the pot, add salt and water, cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is flavorful. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali or rice.

description: Whole tilapia simmered with plenty of onions until the fish is tender and the onions become sweet and silky—a Lakeside classic.

steps.instruction: Clean and score the tilapia. Rub with salt and set aside.
Heat oil in a wide pan and sauté the sliced onions on medium-low heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the chopped tomato (if using) and cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Place the tilapia on top of the onions, add water, cover and simmer for 10–12 minutes until the fish is cooked through. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and greens.

description: Fried tilapia simmered in a thick, tangy tomato sauce—a favourite way to enjoy fresh fish from Lake Victoria.

steps.instruction: Clean and score the tilapia, rub with salt and fry in hot oil for 3–4 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, sauté the onion and garlic until soft.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook on medium heat for 8–10 minutes until they form a thick sauce.
Return the fish to the pan, add water, cover and simmer for 8–10 minutes until the fish is heated through and coated in the sauce. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali or rice.

description: Crispy little omena simmered in a tangy tomato and onion sauce—a protein-packed Kenyan classic from the lake region.

steps.instruction: Rinse the omena and dry-fry in a pan for 3–4 minutes to remove excess moisture and crisp them slightly. Set aside.
Heat oil and sauté the onions until golden. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook on medium heat for 8–10 minutes until they break down into a thick sauce.
Add the omena and salt, stir well and simmer for 5 minutes until the fish is coated and heated through. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali.

name_en: Ngunja Matu (One-Pot Maize Flour and Beans)
description: A traditional Embu and Meru one-pot meal where maize flour is cooked together with beans and greens into a thick, firm, ugali-like dish.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a heavy pot and add the cooked beans. Stir for 2 minutes.
Add water and salt and bring to a boil.
Gradually add the maize flour while stirring continuously with a wooden spoon to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat and keep stirring and folding for 10–12 minutes until the mixture is thick, firm and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Shape into a mound and serve hot with a side of greens or stew.

serving_suggestion: Serve with sukuma wiki or a light stew.

description: Tender beans simmered with sweet, golden onions—a simple, comforting Kenyan stew that lets the onions do the talking.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a pot and add the sliced onions. Cook on medium-low heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the chopped tomato (if using) and cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the cooked beans, salt and water. Stir well and simmer for 15 minutes until the stew thickens and the flavours meld.
Serve hot with ugali, rice or chapati.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali or chapati.

description: Beans cooked in a rich, tangy tomato sauce with onions and a hint of garlic—a Kenyan staple that pairs with everything.

steps.instruction: Heat oil and sauté the onion (if using) until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook on medium heat for 10 minutes until they break down into a thick sauce.
Add the cooked beans and salt. Stir and simmer for 10–15 minutes until the beans are well coated and the sauce is thick.
Serve hot with rice, ugali or chapati.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or ugali.

name_en: Kenyan Green Grams and Onion Stew
description: Soft green grams cooked with plenty of onions until they melt into a savoury, comforting stew.

steps.instruction: Rinse the green grams and boil in water for 25–30 minutes until soft.
In a separate pan, heat oil and sauté the sliced onions on medium-low heat for 10 minutes until golden and sweet.
Add the garlic and tomatoes (if using) and cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes soften.
Add the cooked green grams with a little of their cooking liquid. Simmer for 10 minutes, season with salt and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

description: Green grams simmered in creamy coconut milk with onions and mild spices—a coastal Kenyan favourite.

steps.instruction: Rinse the green grams. Heat oil and sauté the onion and garlic until soft.
Stir in the curry powder and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the green grams, coconut milk, water and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20–25 minutes until the grams are soft and the stew is creamy.
Serve hot with rice or chapati.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

name_sw: Ugali ya Maziwa na Maharagwe ya Siagi
description: Soft, milky ugali served with beans tossed in butter—a comforting Kenyan combination where maize flour and beans come together on one plate.

steps.instruction: Bring water and salt to a boil. Gradually add the maize flour while stirring to prevent lumps.
Add the milk and continue stirring and folding for 8–10 minutes until the ugali is firm and pulls away from the pot.
In a separate pan, melt the butter and toss the cooked beans in it until heated through and glossy.
Serve the milky ugali hot with the buttered beans alongside.

serving_suggestion: Serve with a side of greens.

name_en: Mseto wa Maharagwe (One-Pot Rice and Beans)
description: A common Kenyan one-pot dish of rice cooked together with beans and a tomato-onion base—hearty, economical and deeply satisfying.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a pot and sauté the onion until golden. Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they form a sauce.
Add the cooked beans and stir until coated in the tomato mixture.
Add the washed rice, salt and water. Stir once, then cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff gently with a fork and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with kachumbari or a side of greens.

description: Fragrant rice cooked in coconut milk—the definitive coastal Kenyan side dish, perfumed and slightly sweet.

steps.instruction: Rinse the rice and drain. Heat oil and sauté the onion (if using) until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the coconut milk, water and salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with fish curry or bean stew.

description: Kenya's beloved braised collard greens, cooked with plenty of onions until tender and sweet.

steps.instruction: Wash and finely slice the collard greens. Heat oil and sauté the sliced onions on medium-low heat for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the chopped tomato (if using) and cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the greens and salt. Stir-fry for 5–7 minutes until tender but still bright green.
Serve hot with ugali or any main dish.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and a meat stew.

description: A quick, colourful Kenyan stir-fry of shredded cabbage and sweet carrot, lightly seasoned and perfect alongside ugali.

steps.instruction: Shred the cabbage finely and grate or julienne the carrots.
Heat oil and sauté the onion (if using) until soft.
Add the carrots and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the cabbage and salt.
Stir-fry for 6–8 minutes until the vegetables are tender but still crunchy. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali or chapati.

description: A traditional Luhya dish of boiled sweet potatoes mashed with cooked beans—simple, nutritious and deeply comforting.

steps.instruction: Peel the sweet potatoes and cut into chunks. Boil in salted water for 15–20 minutes until soft. Drain, reserving a little water.
Add the cooked beans to the hot sweet potatoes and mash together until well combined but still slightly chunky.
If the mixture is too dry, add a splash of the reserved cooking water. Adjust salt to taste.
Serve warm on its own or with a stew of your choice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with tea or a light stew.

description: Eggs fried with ripe tomatoes until the two meld into a soft, savoury scramble—a quick Kenyan breakfast or light meal.

steps.instruction: Beat the eggs with salt. Heat oil and sauté the onion (if using) until soft.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 4–5 minutes until they soften and release their juices.
Pour in the beaten eggs and cook on low heat, stirring gently, until the eggs are just set.
Serve hot with ugali, chapati or bread.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and sukuma wiki.

description: Soft scrambled eggs cooked with sweet, golden onions—a simple Kenyan breakfast often served with ugali.

steps.instruction: Finely chop the onion. Heat oil and sauté the onion on medium-low heat for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Beat the eggs with salt and pour over the onions.
Cook on low heat, stirring gently with a spatula, until the eggs are softly scrambled.
Serve immediately with ugali or bread.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali or chapati.

description: A rich, nutty Kenyan stew of spinach simmered with groundnuts, tomatoes and onions—hearty, vegan and full of protein.

steps.instruction: Roast the groundnuts lightly, then grind into a coarse paste or powder.
Heat oil and sauté the onion until golden. Add the garlic and chopped tomatoes and cook until the tomatoes soften.
Add the groundnut paste and water, stirring to combine. Simmer for 8–10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the spinach and salt and cook for 5 minutes until wilted. Serve hot with rice or ugali.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice, ugali or chapati.

description: Tender pigeon peas simmered in creamy coconut milk with onions and a touch of spice—a coastal Kenyan staple.

steps.instruction: Rinse the pigeon peas and boil in water for 25–30 minutes until tender. Drain, reserving the cooking liquid.
Heat oil and sauté the onion and garlic until soft. Stir in the curry powder.
Add the cooked pigeon peas, coconut milk and a little reserved liquid. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until the stew thickens.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or chapati.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

name_en: Kenyan Lentil and Minced Beef Stew
name_sw: Mchuzi wa Dengu na Nyama ya Kuchonga
description: A hearty Kenyan stew combining lentils and minced beef with plenty of onions—protein-rich, economical and deeply flavourful.

steps.instruction: Heat oil and sauté the sliced onions on medium-low heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and curry powder and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the tomatoes (if using) and cook until softened.
Add the lentils-or-minced-beef blend and stir to coat with the onion mixture.
Pour in the water and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20–25 minutes until the lentils and meat are tender and the stew has thickened. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice, ugali or chapati.
